test_title: PYST 26: Selection Post (Higher Secondary Level) - GA (Held On 2 Aug 2022 Shift 2)
subject: gk
question: Select the correct statement from the given options.

options.text: The wind blowing in the western ghats in winters is known as Loo.
The wind blowing in the northern plains in summers is known as Trade winds.
The wind blowing in the coastal areas in winters is known as Loo.
The wind blowing in the northern plains in summers is known as Loo.

solution:
The correct answer is** __The wind blowing in the northern plains in summers is known as Loo.__**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **Loo is the name of the summertime breeze** that blows across the northern plains. A loo is a summer afternoon wind that blows over the western Indo-Gangetic Plain region of** North India and Pakistan**. It is a strong, hot, and dry wind that originates in the west. **May and June are very good months for it.**
 
• The** highlands of north India block any cold air** from the higher latitudes from entering throughout the summer. Therefore, the northwest region and the Indo-Gangetic Plains are exposed to** regular heat waves due to the dry, hot, and dusty winds** that sweep across these **regions.**
 
• During the **colder months,** it blows from the** northeast, and during the hottest months of the year**, it switches directions to blow from the** southwest. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ​​​In the** northern plains, summertime weather is hot and muggy**. 45 to 50 degrees are reached, which could result in **sunstroke.**
 
• Loo: Thunderstorms in **West Bengal and Assam. **Kalbaisakhi: Hot, dry winds from Rajasthan to Western U.P.
 
• Loo has spread to new regions, and is presently raging over **West Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, Gujarat, and Maharashtra**. Furthermore, there are heat wave conditions in **some areas of this region. **

83:T
